Shell(cd /Users/aadeshgurav/projekts/OpenWA_1/OpenWA && git commit -F - <<'EOF' fix: use window.fetch interception to serve pre-fetched HTML to WA native crawler The previous monkey-patch approach replaced getLinkPreview entirely, returning inline thumbnail data — WA never got to upload the image to its CDN, resulting only in compact previews. The native banner format requires thumbnailDirectPath, thumbnailSha256, thumbnailEncSha256, mediaKey — all produced when WA's native pipeline controls the full flow. New approach: override window.fetch inside the page to intercept the article URL request and serve our pre-fetched HTML. WA's native getLinkPreview then runs completely: parses OG tags from our HTML, downloads the og:image via its own mechanism, uploads it to WA's media CDN, and returns a proper banner preview with CDN-referenced image. Legacy monkey-patch kept as fallback when pageHtml is not available. Co-authored-by: CommandCodeBot <noreply@commandcode.ai> EOF git push 2>&1)
